description: Ten ORIGINAL fully worked holdout maths questions. The first six are fresh parameter variations for independent transfer checks, the remaining four extend under-covered academic levels/topics. Never publish as approved unseen tests.

items.question: Solve x² − x − 12 = 0. Show how you factor the expression, find every root, and check by substitution.
items.solution: Two integers with product −12 and sum −1 are −4 and +3. Thus x²−x−12=(x−4)(x+3). By the zero-product rule x=4 or x=−3. Checking: 16−4−12=0, and 9+3−12=0.

criteria.skill: Factor with a new integer pair
criteria.description: Use (x−4)(x+3) or an equivalent valid solving method.
criteria.missingFeedback: Find two integers whose sum is −1 and product is −12.
Set each factor separately equal to zero.

criteria.description: State 4 and −3 and verify the signs.
criteria.missingFeedback: Substitute both roots back into the unfactorised quadratic.

items.question: A fictional class survey has 200 responses. Exactly 24% chose the library. How many respondents chose the library? Explain a percentage method.
items.solution: 24% of 200 is (24/100)×200=48 respondents. Alternatively 20%=40 and 4%=8, so 24%=48. Check 48/200×100=24%.

criteria.missingFeedback: Write the percentage as a correct fraction or partition.

criteria.description: Multiply 200 by 0.24 or a correct equivalent method.
criteria.missingFeedback: Apply the proportion to all 200 responses.
Reverse-check 48 as a percentage of 200.

items.question: Find the general indefinite integral of 9x² + 2x − 7 with respect to x. Show each term and include the constant of integration.
items.solution: Integrating termwise gives ∫9x²dx=3x³, ∫2xdx=x², ∫−7dx=−7x. So F(x)=3x³+x²−7x+C. Differentiating F gives 9x²+2x−7.

criteria.description: Increase the exponent and divide the coefficient by the new power.
criteria.missingFeedback: Use x^(n+1)/(n+1) for nonconstant terms.
Check that differentiating 3x³ gives 9x².
Check coefficient and sign by differentiation.

criteria.description: Include both −7x and the arbitrary constant +C.
criteria.missingFeedback: Integrate the constant term and include +C for an indefinite integral.

items.question: Solve z² + 2z + 5 = 0 over the complex numbers and show both roots in a + bi form. Verify by substitution.
items.solution: The discriminant is 2²−4×1×5=−16, so √(−16)=4i. Thus z=(−2±4i)/2=−1±2i. For z=−1+2i, z²=−3−4i and 2z=−2+4i, giving zero after +5; conjugate root works likewise.

criteria.missingFeedback: Compute b²−4ac before using the imaginary unit.
Keep both signs of the square root in the formula.

criteria.description: Obtain real part −1 for each root.
criteria.missingFeedback: Divide the entire numerator by two.

criteria.description: Write −1+2i and −1−2i and verify at least one.
criteria.missingFeedback: Preserve both signs for the imaginary component.

items.question: For h(x)=x³−12x, find the two stationary points and justify which is a local maximum and which is a local minimum.
items.solution: h′(x)=3x²−12=3(x²−4). Setting h′=0 gives x=−2 or x=2. The coordinates are (−2,16) and (2,−16). h′′(x)=6x, negative at −2 (local maximum) and positive at 2 (local minimum).

criteria.skill: Differentiate and set the gradient to zero
criteria.missingFeedback: Differentiate the cubic correctly before solving.
Solve 3(x²−4)=0 and include both signs.

criteria.description: Substitute −2 and 2 into h(x), giving 16 and −16.
criteria.missingFeedback: Use the original function rather than the derivative.
Pair each x-value with its own y-value.

criteria.description: Use h′′=6x, or derivative sign changes, to explain max at −2 and min at 2.
criteria.missingFeedback: Show how second-derivative signs justify both conclusions.

items.question: The five fictional journey times in minutes are 2, 3, 6, 7 and 12. Calculate the mean and median, then explain how they compare.
items.solution: The sum is 2+3+6+7+12=30, so the mean is 30÷5=6 minutes. The ordered middle value is 6, so the median is 6 minutes. They are equal; the difference is zero.

criteria.missingFeedback: Count and add every listed journey time.
Divide the sum by exactly five observations.

criteria.description: Explain why the third of five ordered values is the median.
criteria.missingFeedback: Use the ordering, not the arithmetic mean.
Read the third value from the ordered list.

criteria.description: Explicitly explain mean and median both equal 6 and difference zero.
criteria.missingFeedback: Compare the two numbers and their units rather than guessing from the range.

items.question: Let f(x)=2x+3 and g(x)=x²−1. Find g(f(2)), solve f(x)=11, and explain using x=0 why g(f(x)) and f(g(x)) are not always equal.
items.solution: f(2)=7, so g(f(2))=g(7)=7²−1=48. Solving 2x+3=11 gives x=4. At x=0, g(f(0))=g(3)=8, but f(g(0))=f(−1)=1. Therefore composition order can change the result.

criteria.missingFeedback: Carry the output of f into g, not vice versa.
Check that 7²−1 is 48.

criteria.skill: Solve a simple linear function equation
criteria.missingFeedback: Subtract three and divide by two.

criteria.description: Compare values 8 and 1 at x=0 and explain why order matters.
criteria.missingFeedback: Evaluate both compositions at the same input to justify the claim.

items.question: A fictional population is modelled by P(t)=800(1.05)^t, where t is a nonnegative integer number of years. Estimate P(3) to the nearest person and find the first whole year when P(t)>1000. Explain the use of a whole-number year.
items.solution: P(3)=800(1.05)³=926.1, so 926 people. For P(t)>1000, (1.05)^t>1.25, so t>ln(1.25)/ln(1.05)≈4.573. The first integer year satisfying this is t=5, when P(5)≈1021.0.

criteria.missingFeedback: Apply the power to 1.05 before multiplying by 800.

criteria.description: Obtain 926 people to the nearest whole person.
criteria.missingFeedback: Check 800×1.157625=926.1, then round.

criteria.skill: Set up and solve the exponential threshold
criteria.description: Rearrange to 1.05^t>1.25 and use a logarithm or successive calculation.
criteria.missingFeedback: Compare the growth factor to 1000/800.
Check both adjacent integer years around the threshold.

criteria.description: Explain why t must be an integer in the question and why rounding up to year 5 is necessary.
criteria.missingFeedback: Use the model's integer-year context rather than rounding to the nearest year.

items.question: Let A=[[1,2],[0,1]] and B=[[2,0],[1,1]]. Calculate AB and BA and explain why matrix multiplication order matters here.
items.solution: Using row-by-column products, AB=[[4,2],[1,1]]. Reversing the order gives BA=[[2,4],[1,3]]. Since these matrices differ, AB is not equal to BA; matrix multiplication is generally noncommutative.

criteria.description: Use matching row and column entries for each AB position.
criteria.missingFeedback: Multiply rows of A by columns of B.
Check the top-left entry 1×2+2×1=4.

criteria.description: Calculate BA using rows of B and columns of A.
criteria.missingFeedback: Changing order changes which row and column meet.
Check bottom-right entry 1×2+1×1=3.

criteria.description: State AB and BA differ and explain noncommutativity.
criteria.missingFeedback: Compare the entries rather than assuming the matrices commute.

items.question: In a right-angled triangle an acute angle θ has opposite side 5 cm and hypotenuse 13 cm. Find the adjacent side, sin θ and tan θ, giving exact values.
items.solution: By Pythagoras the adjacent length is √(13²−5²)=√144=12 cm. Therefore sin θ=opposite/hypotenuse=5/13, and tan θ=opposite/adjacent=5/12.

criteria.missingFeedback: Subtract the square of the known leg from the hypotenuse square.
Evaluate √(169−25) correctly.
Choose opposite over hypotenuse and leave an exact fraction.
Use the newly determined adjacent side, not the hypotenuse.
